newsitem.title: USA: HealthSouth seen a year from full benefits.
newsitem.headline: HealthSouth seen a year from full benefits.

text.p: HealthSouth Corp is not expected to begin reaping the full financial benefits of its newly announced $1.6 billion merger with Horizon/CMS Healthcare Corp until mid-1998, analysts said on Tuesday.

HealthSouth Chairman Richard Scrushy told analysts he hoped to squeeze $10-20 million in costs from obvious areas such as the two companies' legal and accounting operations within six months of an expected mid-year closing date.

Analysts also said that they believe HealthSouth will wind up selling off most most of Horizon's nursing homes as the Birmingham, Ala.-based firm concentrates on improving profitability among its newly acquired rehabilitation centers.

Scrushy projected $40-50 million in additional revenues over the short term simply from moving higher-yielding private HealthSouth patients through Horizon facilities and reducing the rate of low-yielding Medicare patients within the Horizon system.
But analysts say the more substantial improvements will take more time.
"The easiest part to accomplish is the cost-cutting side and some of that you can probably accomplish in the first six months after you close the deal," said PaineWebber's Helen O'Donnell.

"Then the other part is building the revenue side, which is where they bring their contracts to Horizon hospitals, and that'll take a longer time to build. They'll start getting some benefits in about 12 months."
An initial task would be to raise the occupancy rate in Horizon's rehabilitation hospitals that currently runs about 10-15 basis points below the HealthSouth occupancy rate.
"You may not close that gap entirely in 12 months, but you'll probably start inching up the Horizon occupancy," O'Donnell said.
Scrushy avoided comments about the prospect of asset sales. But he clearly laid out how the merger would help achieve two main planks in the HealthSouth strategy.
First, the deal lets HealthSouth into another 50 major metropolitan markets from which it had been excluded by franchise agreements up to now.

Scrushy said entrance into these market, which bring HealthSouth's reach to 250 metroplitan areas in all 50 states, would enable the company to get new contracts with large existing clients such as Wal-Mart Stores Inc, Marriott International Inc and Coca-Cola Co.

But he also said the move would put HealthSouth in the best position to take advantage of anticipated reforms in Medicare, which he said would enable the company to make money for the first time from the goverment-sponsored health-care plan for the elderly.
"As we see Medicare recipients move into a managed-care environment, we're going to be sitting there in every major city in America positioned to contract for it," he said.
The HealthSouth goal also would be to continue growing until it has entered the 300 top U.S. metropolitan markets.
"Hopefully, over the next 10 years, we'll be in every major city with all services," Scrushy added.
"That would generate about $25 billion in sales. And that's our goal -- to build a company that is in every major market."
